newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 30.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
- Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin pledges more economic and political reforms and holds high late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping's banner of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
- Urban per capita living space rises to 8.22 square metres.
- China executes eight in northwestern Moslem region of Xinjiang for staging a spate of bombings, murders and robbers that left 18 people dead.
- China restricts import of equipment to manufacture laser disks by requiring such imports to apply for licences, but abolishes similar requirement for import of pesticides and carbonic drinks.
- Vice-Premier Li Lanqing calls for measures to regulate exports of cocoon and silk.
- Ministry of Public Security to crack down on theft and smuggling of relics.
- 1,997 gold pens to be sold for 7,997 each to mark Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
- Survey shows 55 percent of Beijing residents do not believe in fortune telling.
- Survey shows 66.94 percent of Chinese men and 4.19 percent of women smoke.
- Foreign investment in 18 of China's coastal and border regions decrease in first quarter of 1997.
